assumptions: The envelope grammar uses CBOR maps with exact named fields and preserves arbitrary field order. Serde's additional sequence representations are a dependency boundary, while the published map form is covered.

The source extractor accepts a closed Rust grammar for integer_width, update_budget and the checked atomic request frontier. Generated Lean certificates quantify the width, appended integer bytes and allocator arithmetic. Truncation/header statements pass a closed syntax check; prefix and frame replacement require a valid old frame, offset and representable length. Complete unchanged functions also execute in the probe. Rust Vec, casts, atomic linearization, compiler and extractor correctness are explicit translation boundaries.

Frame theorems range over arbitrary finite bodies, tails, message lists and chunk partitions, subject to configured maximum and u32 length bounds. Transport fairness and eventual byte delivery remain environment properties.

The current protocol has fixed UP/1 compatibility and an invoke_budget_v1 capability. The hello relation records acceptance of version 1; it does not introduce version-range negotiation or same-connection reconnection.

Rust allocates successful request IDs from 1 through u64::MAX-1 and rejects exhaustion without wrapping. Python integers and TypeScript bigint frontiers increase without arithmetic wrap; their value validators enforce the wire u64 range.

Events are completed event-loop sections or lock-linearized transport actions. The shared Session trace distinguishes queue admission, positive write, write completion, response settlement and return.

The request's received result remains owned by the coroutine until successful return. Python finally closes a settled result when cancellation or send failure wins before return; TypeScript catch closes received when Promise.all fails.

The finite Python probe runs the full production request and response methods with real asyncio Task/Future scheduling and a controlled send. The finite TypeScript probe executes the whole source Connection class using Node TypeScript transform, real Promise/Map/AbortController/timers, and explicit CBOR, payload and transport adapters.

Cancellation follows active await or inherited signal edges supplied by each runtime. The descendant theorem covers every member of the supplied descendant list; discovery of that runtime graph and scheduler fairness remain environment boundaries.

Deadline timestamps share one monotone clock. Duration conversion, floating-clock precision and millisecond rounding are separate representation boundaries; the shrinking budget order is proved over natural ticks.

Parses is an independent byte grammar. Its recursive values include scalar integers, IEEE float bits, valid UTF-8 text, arbitrary byte strings, arrays, arbitrary-key ordered maps and tags. It includes all argument widths, half/single/double float productions, indefinite containers and segmented byte/text input.

The structural roundtrip proves parsing of arbitrary bounded recursive values in this grammar, including suffix preservation. It is not an arbitrary-program equivalence theorem for the entire ciborium byte parser, serde visitor, UTF-8 library or Rust compiler.

FloatCodec is the fixed dependency interpretation of IEEE conversions. The model quantifies over every bit pattern and only allows narrowing after exact expanded-bit equality; primitive results fit their u16/u32 widths. Source reflection checks both ciborium float guards and the integer/tag predicates; finite codec probes independently cover NaN payloads, infinities, subnormals and signed zero.

CBOR tags 2 and 3 with definite byte strings of at most 16 bytes have integer semantics in ciborium. Negative magnitudes at least 2^127 reject; larger byte strings remain ordinary tags. The integer theorems compose byte parsing with this interpretation, and do not claim raw Value::Tag constructor identity for numeric tags.

The u128/i128 witness encodings use legal fixed 16-byte bignum bodies. The dependency may remove leading zero bytes; the semantic interpretation agrees, while byte-for-byte canonical equality is not asserted.

Codec limits, persistent resource exclusion and resource tag shape are explicit value-tree policies. Operating-system allocation, panic behavior and recursive parser implementation remain separate dependency boundaries.

Recursive normalization is applied before resource validation for the definite-length encodings generated by the model. Indefinite byte bodies under tags 2/3 retain their wire-form distinction in the dependency parser and are checked independently; the normalized-encoding relation is restricted to generated definite-length encodings.

MathValue integer leaves range from i128::MIN through u128::MAX. The recursive lowering theorem preserves mathematical integers throughout arrays, map keys/values and ordinary tags, proves Fits and a normalization fixed point, and composes with the byte grammar. Ordinary tag 2/3 requires a body outside the short definite byte-string numeric form; successful decode additionally requires the resource policy. Leading-zero removal is proved to preserve magnitude and the 16-byte bound.
